evidence_schema: Flat NDJSON; integer numbers, lowercase byte hex strings, semicolon-delimited integer lists; records scoped by backend
history_rule: Row-major o_idx*n_states entries; -1 denotes invalid/unread history; only initialized predecessor bytes are observed. ae_next is empty before the first nonempty scan/flush, otherwise its complete initialized array is observed, including retention across reset/rewind.
buffer_rule: Byte hex preserves signed soft-bit bit patterns. Outputs begin as a5 bytes and include four untouched suffix bytes (raw/flush buffers also retain unwritten capacity). Empty strings represent absent buffers. Void operations omit ret except load_state, which records ret=0 as a harness placeholder, not a C return.
sequence_rule: Each backend/case has consecutive operation seq starting at zero; descriptor keys are backend/id. Generic state is post-operation. Arrays are semantic data, never object memory. Only valid forced/auto traceback is emitted. Non-tail no-survivor auto output returns -1 before accessing history.
soft_modes: 0=clean +/-127;1=zeros;2=every-fifth sign flip, otherwise +/-31;3=clean with -128 for encoded one;4=cyclic -1,0,1 ties;5=all -128
golden_exclusions: Unsafe shift/sizing probes emit diagnostics only in --audit. Short fixed-start tail-biting fallback is omitted below K; empty non-flush fallback is omitted. Zero-length flush fallback and short non-tail calls are observed. K>9 generic snapshots and one-shot tail-biting are omitted because byte states leave unreachable history; K=10 encoding/load-state and safe non-tail fallback are observed.

coverage.exhaustive: Every length-0..4 bit pattern for N=2,K=3; tail-biting begins at length 2
coverage.recursion: Explicit systematic and nonsystematic descriptors, including -EPROTO
coverage.normalization: N=2..4,K=5/7; total trellis lengths interval-1,interval,interval+1,3*interval+1; recursion absent/systematic/nonsystematic; six soft modes
coverage.known_vector_assertions: GMR-1 TCH3 Speech;WiMax FCH;fixture-only unchanged upstream tables and packed vectors
